verdicts.tldr: serve hands back the listener, so http.Server.Close never runs and the Serve error is dropped
verdicts.details: shots.go:158 builds srv := &http.Server{...}, shots.go:162 runs go srv.Serve(ln) with the error discarded, and shots.go:163 returns ln as the io.Closer, so no reference to the *http.Server survives serve(). The deferred closes at shots.go:61 and shots.go:127 therefore close the listener and never call http.Server.Close, which is what drains tracked connections. A Serve that fails after a successful bind is silent, and every chromeShot then reports Chrome's own connection error instead of the real cause. The process exits moments later, so nothing outlives it. Fix: return a Closer whose Close calls srv.Close(), and log the Serve error when it is not http.ErrServerClosed.
verdicts.evidence: read shots.go:153-163: `srv := &http.Server{Handler: http.FileServer(http.Dir(dir)), ReadHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second}`, `go srv.Serve(ln) //nolint:errcheck`, `return ln, "http://" + ln.Addr().String(), nil`; callers at shots.go:61 and shots.go:127 are `defer srv.Close()` on that returned io.Closer, and grep for srv.Close/srv.Shutdown in the package finds no other site.
verdicts.verify_by: read shots.go:153-163 against shots.go:61 and shots.go:127: the value named srv at the call sites is the listener, and no reference to the *http.Server survives serve().

verdicts.tldr: the PR comment links realms gnodev never rendered, so a reviewer clicks a 404 with nothing saying it failed
verdicts.details: Comment's signature at comment.go:17 takes no *Crawler, and the changed-realm loop at comment.go:62-63 plus the indirect loop at comment.go:79-80 emit a page link, a _t/source/ and a _t/help/ for every entry of p.ChangedRealms and p.Realms unconditionally. Index at comment.go:170 does guard each row with c.pages[u], so the two surfaces disagree. main.go never prunes plan.Realms between the crawl at main.go:134 and Comment at main.go:156, so a realm the crawler skipped on a non-200 or a transport error (crawl.go:130-137) stays in the plan and reaches the comment. Fix: pass the Crawler into Comment and either skip a realm absent from c.pages or mark it as failed to render.
verdicts.evidence: read comment.go:17 `func Comment(p *Plan, baseURL, pr string) string` against comment.go:166 `func Index(p *Plan, c *Crawler) string` and its guard at 170 `if _, ok := c.pages[u]; !ok { continue }`; grep over main.go shows plan.Realms assigned only in plan.go (261, 266) and never filtered after c.Run() at main.go:134, with Index(plan, c) at 141 and Comment(plan, ...) at 156. The finder's b5 fixture reproduces it: body carries the r/x/failed link while Index emitted no row for it.
verdicts.verify_by: cp the artifact and run `go test ./... -run TestB5CommentLinksUncapturedRealm -v` in misc/gnopreview

verdicts.tldr: the sticky-comment marker lives twice, so editing the Go const posts a second preview comment on every open PR
verdicts.details: comment.go:10-12 documents CommentMarker as what the publishing job matches on, while .github/workflows/pr-preview-publish.yml:169 carries its own literal marker='<!-- gnoweb-pr-preview -->' and nothing ties the two. The only test touching the const, plan_test.go:196, asserts the body contains CommentMarker whatever its value, so changing it compiles and stays green. The job then finds no github-actions[bot] comment containing its own literal, takes the else branch at pr-preview-publish.yml:177 and creates a fresh comment on each push, which is exactly the duplication the const exists to prevent. Fix: have the workflow read the marker from the tool or from the first line of comment.md instead of repeating the literal.
verdicts.evidence: grep -rn 'gnoweb-pr-preview' over misc/gnopreview and .github/workflows returns two independent sites: comment.go:12 `const CommentMarker = ...` and pr-preview-publish.yml:169 `marker='<!-- gnoweb-pr-preview -->'`. grep over the test files returns one hit, plan_test.go:196 `CommentMarker,` used as a contains-substring expectation, so no test pins the value.
verdicts.verify_by: grep -rn 'gnoweb-pr-preview' misc/gnopreview .github/workflows — two independent literals; change the const and run `cd misc/gnopreview && go test ./...` to see it stay green

verdicts.tldr: Pkg.Draft is parsed for every package on every run and read nowhere, so draft realms are previewed like any other
verdicts.details: grep -rn 'Draft' over misc/gnopreview returns exactly two lines, the field declaration at plan.go:58 and the assignment at plan.go:142; nothing reads it and Pkg carries no json tags, so it is not serialized out either. modFlags' doc at plan.go:153 calls them the two booleans we care about, while only Ignore reaches a filter, at plan.go:220 and plan.go:241. Either the field and half of modFlags are dead code, or draft packages were meant to be excluded from the preview and are not. Fix: decide which, then drop Draft with its parse branch or filter on it beside Ignore.
verdicts.evidence: grep -rn 'Draft' /…/misc/gnopreview/ → plan.go:58 `Draft   bool     // gnomod.toml: draft = true` and plan.go:142 `pkg.Draft, pkg.Ignore = modFlags(...)`. No third hit, tests included.
verdicts.verify_by: grep -rn "Draft" misc/gnopreview — expect a reader, observe only the declaration and the assignment

verdicts.tldr: `make run` leaves misc/gnopreview/_preview.changed in every contributor's git status
verdicts.details: git check-ignore -v --no-index in the head worktree matches misc/gnopreview/_preview/x against .gitignore:14:_preview/ and matches misc/gnopreview/_preview.changed against nothing at all. The tool's own Makefile writes that file in its run target, `git -C $(GNOROOT) diff --name-only $(BASE)... > $(OUT).changed` with OUT ?= _preview, and its clean target removes it beside _preview/, which is the author's own statement that it is a build leftover. It then shows as untracked for the rest of the session and a git add -A commits that developer's changed-file list. Fix: ignore _preview.changed beside _preview/ on .gitignore:14.
verdicts.evidence: git check-ignore -v --no-index misc/gnopreview/_preview.changed misc/gnopreview/_preview/x printed one line only, `.gitignore:14:_preview/	misc/gnopreview/_preview/x`; grep -n 'changed|_preview' .gitignore returns only line 14. Makefile lines 6, 14 and 27: `OUT ?= _preview`, `> $(OUT).changed`, `rm -rf $(OUT) $(OUT).changed`.
verdicts.verify_by: cd <head worktree> && git check-ignore -v --no-index misc/gnopreview/_preview.changed misc/gnopreview/_preview/x — the second matches `.gitignore:14:_preview/`, the first matches nothing; `sed -n '6,20p' misc/gnopreview/Makefile` shows `OUT ?= _preview`, `> $(OUT).changed` in `run` and `rm -rf $(OUT) $(OUT).changed` in `clean`

verdicts.tldr: the cap warning counts as missing up to four seed realms the preview actually rendered
verdicts.details: plan.go:256-258 sets plan.Dropped = len(realms) - maxRealms and truncates, then plan.go:263-269 appends any gnowebSeedRealms absent from the truncated slice back into plan.Realms without touching Dropped. comment.go:85-86 prints that stale count as N more affected realm(s) were not rendered (cap reached), so a realm sitting in the preview is reported as lost, by up to len(gnowebSeedRealms). It needs plan.Gnoweb set, more affected realms than maxRealms, and a seed in the truncated tail — reachable since the seeds sort under gno.land/r/docs/ and gno.land/r/gnoland/, after the gno.land/r/demo/ block. Fix: compute Dropped after the seed append, from the realms actually absent from plan.Realms.
verdicts.evidence: read plan.go:256-270: `plan.Dropped = len(realms) - maxRealms` and `realms = realms[:maxRealms]` precede `if plan.Gnoweb { for _, r := range gnowebSeedRealms { if pkgs[r] != nil && !contains(plan.Realms, r) { plan.Realms = append(plan.Realms, r) } } }`; no assignment to plan.Dropped exists after line 257, and comment.go:86 is its only reader.
verdicts.verify_by: BuildPlan with gnoweb changed, maxRealms below the affected count and gno.land/r/gnoland/home among the truncated affected realms: expect Dropped to exclude it, observe it counted while present in plan.Realms

verdicts.tldr: an unreadable gnomod.toml silently previews a package that asked to be ignored
verdicts.details: LoadPkgs sets hasMod from the directory listing at plan.go:125, so modFlags runs only on a file already known to exist, and plan.go:156-158 turns every read error into false, false with nothing on stderr. An ignore = true package whose file cannot be read — permissions, a dangling symlink, a truncated checkout — then passes the Ignore filters at plan.go:220 and plan.go:241 and is booted into gnodev and rendered, the opposite of what the file asked for. The trigger needs a damaged tree, so this is latent rather than something the workflow will hit. Fix: return the error from modFlags, or at least print it, instead of reporting the package as neither draft nor ignored.
verdicts.evidence: read plan.go:155-159: `b, err := os.ReadFile(p); if err != nil { return false, false }`, reached from plan.go:142 only under the `hasMod` branch established at plan.go:125-133 (`if !hasMod || len(files) == 0 { return nil }`). The two consumers are plan.go:220 `if p := byDir[path.Dir(f)]; p != nil && !p.Ignore` and plan.go:241 `if !pkgs[p].Realm || pkgs[p].Ignore { continue }`.
verdicts.verify_by: chmod 000 on an ignore = true gnomod.toml and run BuildPlan: expect the package excluded, observe it in plan.Realms

verdicts.tldr: a -chrome path that does not resolve is ignored and the shots are taken with some other browser, silently
verdicts.details: shots.go:196-200 puts the explicit flag and $CHROME into the same candidate slice as google-chrome, google-chrome-stable, chromium, chromium-browser and the macOS bundle, and the loop at shots.go:201-211 continues past any candidate failing both LookPath and Stat. A typo, or a path absent from the runner image, therefore falls through to whatever browser is installed, with nothing on stderr saying the pinned one was not used. The flag exists to pin a browser, so a version-specific rendering difference between the before and after columns becomes invisible. Fix: when explicit is non-empty and resolves to neither a PATH entry nor a file, return an error naming the path instead of falling through.
verdicts.evidence: read shots.go:195-213: `candidates := []string{explicit, os.Getenv("CHROME")}` then `candidates = append(candidates, "google-chrome", ...)`; the loop body is `if c == "" { continue }`, LookPath, Stat, and the function ends `return ""` — there is no branch distinguishing the explicit entry from the fallbacks.
verdicts.verify_by: read shots.go:195-213: the explicit candidate is one entry of the same slice as the fallbacks, with no error path when it fails both LookPath and Stat

verdicts.tldr: only the listener is closed, so the snapshot server's connections are left to the process exit
verdicts.details: serve at shots.go:153-163 builds the *http.Server at 158 and returns ln, the net.Listener, as its io.Closer; the server value escapes nowhere else in the package. Screenshot at shots.go:127 and ScreenshotPairs at shots.go:61 defer that Closer, so http.Server.Close — the call that closes tracked connections — never runs, and Chrome's keep-alive connection to the snapshot server plus the handler goroutine live until the process exits. The //nolint comment at shots.go:162 speaks to Serve's return value and says nothing about the server's connections. Fix: return an io.Closer whose Close calls srv.Close(), which closes the listener as its side effect.
verdicts.evidence: read shots.go:153-163 and grep for srv.Close/srv.Shutdown across misc/gnopreview: the only Close calls are `defer srv.Close()` at shots.go:61 and shots.go:127, where the identifier srv is bound to serve()'s first return value, the listener.
verdicts.verify_by: read shots.go:153-163: srv is an *http.Server, the returned io.Closer is ln, and nothing calls srv.Close or srv.Shutdown

verdicts.tldr: -max-realms is exceeded by up to four realms on any PR that touches gnoweb, and Dropped says nothing
verdicts.details: plan.go:256-258 applies the cap, and plan.go:263-268 then appends each of the four gnowebSeedRealms not already present, with no cap check, whenever plan.Gnoweb is set. Any diff under gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/, gno.land/cmd/gnoweb/ or contribs/gnodev/ sets that flag (plan.go:28-32, 212-216), so -max-realms=1 renders up to five realms and reports Dropped=0. The knob is what bounds gnodev boot and crawl time in the preview job, and the comment carries no sign of the overrun. Fix: append the seeds before the truncation, or re-apply the cap after appending them.
verdicts.evidence: read plan.go:256-270 — the append loop has no length guard and runs after `realms = realms[:maxRealms]`; the finder's run over a fake repo holding the four seeds gives `max-realms=1 rendered=5 dropped=0 realms=[gno.land/r/docs/security_patterns gno.land/r/gnoland/blog gno.land/r/gnoland/boards2/v0 gno.land/r/gnoland/home gno.land/r/x/leaf]`.
verdicts.verify_by: go test -run TestClaimSeedRealmsBypassCap in misc/gnopreview with a fake repo that contains the four gnowebSeedRealms: BuildPlan(root, ["gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/app.go", "examples/gno.land/p/x/base/v0/lib.gno"], 1) must return 1 realm; observe 5

verdicts.tldr: the index page claims more realms than it lists, and nothing on it says which one failed
verdicts.details: Index's row loop at comment.go:168-172 skips any realm absent from c.pages, while the header at comment.go:191-195 interpolates len(p.Realms). main.go:141 passes the unpruned plan, and plan.Realms is never filtered between the crawl at main.go:134 and that call, so a realm gnodev answered non-200 for (crawl.go:134-137) is counted in the header and missing from the list. A reviewer reads 25 realm(s) rendered above 24 rows with no explanation, and the one realm they came to look at may be the missing one. Fix: count the rows written and name the realms that failed to render.
verdicts.evidence: read comment.go:166-196: `for _, r := range p.Realms { u := urlOf(r); if _, ok := c.pages[u]; !ok { continue }` against the format argument `len(p.Realms)` at line 195; grep over main.go shows no assignment to plan.Realms anywhere, so the count and the rows come from different sets.
verdicts.verify_by: read Index: the row loop skips `if _, ok := c.pages[u]; !ok` while the header interpolates len(p.Realms)

verdicts.tldr: the subtest named for the tests-fixture exclusion would pass with that exclusion deleted
verdicts.details: plan_test.go:42-43 wires gno.land/r/tests/vm/fixture to import gno.land/p/x/base/v0, while the subtest named tests fixtures are not pulled in indirectly changes p/x/mid/v0 at plan_test.go:85. dependents() never reaches the fixture from p/x/mid, so the indirectExclude guard at plan.go:244 is not exercised and its removal leaves that case green. The exclusion is covered in fact, by transitive dependency pulls both dependents and cap keeps the changed realm, whose names say nothing about it, so a later edit narrowing indirectExclude gets debugged against the wrong subtest. Fix: point the fixture's import at gno.land/p/x/mid/v0 so the case named for the exclusion depends on it.
verdicts.evidence: read plan_test.go:32-51 and 83-88: the fixture body is `package fixture\nimport \"gno.land/p/x/base/v0\"` and the subtest's changed list is `examples/gno.land/p/x/mid/v0/lib.gno`; reverse edges in dependents() (plan.go:295-315) reach only p/x/mid/v0 and r/x/leaf from that seed. The finder's mutation of plan.go:244 agrees: that subtest stayed green while cap keeps the changed realm and transitive dependency pulls both dependents went red.
verdicts.verify_by: replace the `!changedPkgs[p] && hasPrefixAny(p, indirectExclude)` guard in plan.go:244 with `_ = indirectExclude` and run go test -run TestBuildPlan: the subtest named for the exclusion must go red
